title: Original manuscript of Gitanjali - Rabindranath Tagore - Rothenstein collection.pdf, notebook page numbered '20' (printed folio '11')
licenseTag: Public Domain Mark 1.0 (CC0-equivalent per file page)
licenseBasis: File page states public domain because the author (Tagore) died in 1941 and the manuscript predates 1931. Source: Rothenstein Papers collection, Houghton Library, Harvard University -- Tagore's autograph manuscript, given to William Rothenstein in London in 1912.
notes: This is page 25 of the 184-page PDF (Commons' internal page-thumbnail numbering), rendered via the MediaWiki PDF page-thumbnail endpoint at the 960px-wide tier (960px was the only thumbnail width Commons would render on demand for this file; larger widths returned HTTP 400). Full source PDF is 175.95MB / 184 pages at native ~1185x1754px per page; this is a downsampled render, not the full-resolution scan. Visually confirmed this specific page shows Tagore's characteristic handwritten revision marks: a word crossed out with 'meet' inserted above the line, another crossed-out word replaced inline with 'sorrow', and a caret-inserted 'forget'. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this manuscript is Tagore's own ENGLISH-language autograph translation of Gitanjali (the version he brought to London in 1912), not a Bengali-script manuscript -- no Bengali-script Gitanjali manuscript scan with visible revision marks was located on Commons. The requested ideal (Bengali-script Gitanjali manuscript with revisions) was not found; this English-language autograph with revisions was substituted as the closest verified match.

title: Title page,『গীতাঞ্জলি』(Gitanjali), original Bengali text, Sri Rabindranath Tagore -- তৃতীয় সংস্করণ (Third Edition), Indian Press, Allahabad, Bengali year ১৩২০ (Bengali Era 1320 = c. 1913 CE)
sourceCollection: Digital Library of India scan, mirrored to Wikimedia Commons as File:গীতাঞ্জলি - রবীন্দ্রনাথ ঠাকুর.djvu (uploaded by Commons user Jayanta Nath)
originalFileUrl: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/04/%E0%A6%97%E0%A7%80%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%9E%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%9C%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BF_-_%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%80%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A5_%E0%A6%A0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0.djvu (page 1 of 190, rendered via MediaWiki djvu page-thumbnail endpoint at 1920px width)
licenseBasis: Commons file categorized PD-old-80-expired and CC-PD-Mark, extmetadata License=pd, UsageTerms=Public domain, AttributionRequired=false. Author Rabindranath Tagore died 1941, well past any life+70/80 term; text itself first published 1910.
pixelSize: 1920x2938 (native djvu page is 2700x4132; Commons' thumbnail renderer capped delivery at 1920px width)
notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT, stated plainly: this is NOT the 1910 first edition. The title page itself reads তৃতীয় সংস্করণ (Third Edition), publisher Indian Press (Allahabad), Bengali year ১৩২০ (Bengali San 1320, which converts to roughly 1913 CE). This Digital Library of India scan was the only PD-licensed original-Bengali-text Gitanjali edition located on Commons; no scan of the true 1910 Kuntaline Press first edition was found there. Flagging for a maintainer: if the 1910-first-edition distinction matters for the art pass, a further targeted search of the Digital Library of India (dli.gov.in successor / archive.org 'Bichitra' Tagore variorum) or the Rabindra Bhavana archive at Visva-Bharati would be needed -- out of scope for this Commons-only pass.

title: Cover, "The Home and the World" (English translation of ঘরে বাইরে / Ghare Baire), Rabindranath Tagore
sourceCollection: Internet Archive (archive.org/details/hometheworld00tagouoft), mirrored to Wikimedia Commons as File:The Home and the World - cover page.jpg
licenseBasis: Commons file categorized PD US, extmetadata License=pd, UsageTerms=Public domain, AttributionRequired=false. Commons' own DateTimeOriginal field records 1921 for this specific scanned copy/printing.
notes: Low resolution -- this is the only size Commons hosts for this file (credited directly to the Internet Archive item, no larger derivative found). archive.org was intermittently unreachable during this research session ('Internet Archive: Temporarily Offline'), so the exact original publisher/print-run details for IA identifier hometheworld00tagouoft could NOT be independently verified beyond what Commons' own extmetadata states (DateTimeOriginal=1921); treat the 1921 date as Commons-sourced, not independently cross-checked against archive.org's own catalog record. The English translation (by Surendranath Tagore, revised by the author) was first published by Macmillan in 1919; this specific digitized copy's printing likely falls close to that but is not confirmed to be the true first printing.
